subtopics.title: Why in News: World Wetlands Day 2026
subtopics.summary: World Wetlands Day is observed on 2 February, and the 2026 theme is 'Wetlands and Traditional Knowledge: Celebrating Cultural Heritage'. India's Ramsar Network was expanded when the Union Environment Minister added two new wetlands, bringing the total to 98. Patna Bird Sanctuary in Etah District, Uttar Pradesh, was recognised as the state's smallest bird sanctuary.
facts: World Wetlands Day is observed on 2 February.
The 2026 theme is Wetlands and Traditional Knowledge: Celebrating Cultural Heritage.
Union Environment Minister added two new wetlands to India's Ramsar Network.
India's Ramsar Network total reaches 98.
Patna Bird Sanctuary is in Etah District, Uttar Pradesh.
Patna Bird Sanctuary was established in 1991.
Patna Bird Sanctuary is recognised as the state's smallest bird sanctuary.
Chhari-Dhand Wetland Reserve is in Gujarat's Rann of Kutch.
Chhari-Dhand is famous for Chir Batti night lights across Banni Grasslands.

subtopics.title: Meaning and Classification of Wetlands
subtopics.summary: A wetland is a place where land is covered by water, which may be salt, fresh or in between, and may be seasonal or permanent. The term covers a wide range of water bodies and coastal habitats, from lakes and rivers to mangroves and coral reefs. For classification, wetlands are grouped into three segments.
facts: Wetland: land covered by water that is salt, fresh or in between.
The water cover may be seasonal or permanent.
Includes lakes, rivers and underground aquifers.
Includes swamps, wet grasslands and peatlands.
Includes deltas, tidal flats and mangroves.
Includes coral reefs and other coastal areas.
Wetlands are classified into three segments.
The three segments are Inland, Coastal and Human-made wetlands.

subtopics.title: Ramsar Convention and Montreux Record
subtopics.summary: The Ramsar Convention, formally the Convention on Wetlands of International Importance, was signed in 1971 in Ramsar, Iran, and came into force in 1975. It is the only international treaty addressing a specific ecosystem, and its Conference of Parties meets every 3 years. The Montreux Record, launched in 1990, lists wetland sites where ecological character has changed or is likely to change due to technological developments, pollution or other human interference.
facts: The Ramsar Convention was signed in 1971 in Ramsar, Iran.
The Convention came into force in 1975.
It is the only international treaty addressing a specific ecosystem.
The Convention has 172 member States.

Keoladeo National Park and Loktak Lake are on the Montreux Record; Chilka Lake was removed.

subtopics.title: Government Initiatives and Wetland City Accreditation
subtopics.summary: Amrit Dharohar is a capacity building scheme between the Ministry of Tourism and the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, aimed at optimal wetland use and nature tourism. The National Wetland Conservation Program is implemented through State Wetland Authorities, and the National Wetland Decadal Change Atlas was prepared by SAC, ISRO. The Wetland City Accreditation Program promotes conservation and wise use of urban and peri-urban wetlands.

quizzes.title: Wetlands and the Ramsar Framework
quizzes.passage: Wetlands are places where land is covered by water, whether the water is salt, fresh or somewhere in between, and whether the cover is seasonal or permanent. The category is broad, and every form of water cover described here is treated as part of one wetland definition. It includes lakes, rivers, underground aquifers, swamps, wet grasslands and peatlands, along with deltas, tidal flats, mangroves, coral reefs and other coastal areas. For classification, wetlands are divided into three segments. The international framework that protects these ecosystems is a treaty that deals with one specific type of habitat. Its formal name is the Convention on Wetlands of International Importance, and it is the only international treaty that addresses a specific ecosystem. Its members meet at a Conference of Parties. Wetland sites that fall under it are known as Ramsar Sites, and India is one of the signatories. A separate register tracks wetland sites where ecological character has changed, is changing, or is likely to change. Such changes can result from technological developments, pollution or other human interference. A site entered on this register shows that its ecological character is under pressure. World Wetlands Day is observed each year, and each year carries its own theme that draws attention to wetland care.

questions.q:
Read the two statements and choose the correct option.
Assertion (A): Human-made wetlands are one of the three segments used to classify wetlands.
Reason (R): Wetlands are defined only as natural water bodies such as lakes and rivers.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet classifies wetlands into three segments, one of which is human-made, so R is false while A is true.

How many of the following statements about the Ramsar Convention are correct?
I. It was signed in 1971 in Ramsar, Iran.
II. It came into force in 1980.
III. India became a signatory on 1 February 1982.

questions.explanation: Statement II is wrong because the Convention came into force in 1975, so statements I, III and IV are correct.

quizzes.title: Schemes, Atlas and Accreditation
quizzes.passage: India's wetland policy combines conservation with tourism and local livelihoods. Under one capacity building scheme, a tourism ministry works with the environment ministry to make better use of wetlands. The scheme aims to enhance biodiversity, carbon stock, eco-tourism opportunities and income for local communities. Its primary focus is a shift from crowded visits to higher-value nature tourism at ecologically sensitive wetlands. Conservation at the national level is carried out through state-level bodies. A national atlas of decadal wetland change documents how these wetlands have changed over time, and an original version of that atlas was released by a national space agency unit. Such records help authorities see which wetlands have altered over a decade. The programme is run jointly, so the planning of wetland use and the study of wetland change are both part of one national effort. Tourism is also being planned along cultural routes. A new corridor will connect Ayodhya with another place in the same state, combining cultural visits with nature, and the corridor is announced as a new route in the state. Cities are recognised too. Wetland City Accreditation is granted only to cities that satisfy all six international criteria, including measures for conservation of wetlands and their ecosystem services. The programme aims to promote conservation and wise use of urban and peri-urban wetlands.
